# Tab 1

# Project Overview

Design small circular PCBs with controllable LEDs which can be connected in a chain. These PCBs will be used to replace lights used to illuminate a collection of small holiday decorations on a shelf.

I prototyped this project by cutting up a flexible LED strip ([image](#image-1:-flexible-led-prototype)), but would like to clean it up using PCBs before giving it to my mom.

## Scope

* Design and layout of PCB schematic and layout  
* Part selection  
* BOM for assembly by JLCPCB (using in-stock components)

# Requirements

1. Every LED on the PCB should display the same colors.  
2. Each PCB of lights should be individually addressable.  
3. Each PCB should contain 3 LEDs.

Each PCB should be addressable, not each LED on a PCB. PCBs will be wired in series.

For example, in the diagram below a controller should be able to independently control Light 1, Light 2, up to Light N. The controller does not need to independently control LED0, LED1, or LED2 on Light 1\.

## LEDs

LEDs should be RGBW, with **WARM WHITE** (\~3000K)

LEDs should support color dimming, and will be controlled by an Arduino or ESP32. Controller design is out of scope of this phase, but may be a future project if this goes well.

LED brightness should be consistent with consumer-grade LED light strips like https://www.adafruit.com/product/2439. The brighter the better.

## Connectors

PCB should contain 1 input and 1 output connector.  
The input connector will carry \+12V, DIN, GND  
The output connector should carry \+12, DOUT, GND

Each connector should be a 3-pin JST-style connector.

# PCB Constraints

**Shape:** Circle  
**Radius:** 10mm  
**Material:** Solid

All LEDs and components must be on Top side, with the exception of connectors, to minimize PCB assembly complexity.

Connectors may be on the Bottom side.
